Flag tokens with too few samples with f0, or with points missing

Source: R/gaps.R
flag_f0_tokens.Rd

Adds a column, screen_flag, that says in a few words what is wrong with each token: "" (empty) for a token with no issue, otherwise its reasons, such as "only 2 samples with f0", the same text on every row of the token. No row is removed: keep the tokens with no issue with data[data$screen_flag == "", ] if wanted. This is what the app's Start page does before its Drop the N flagged tokens box.

Usage

flag_f0_tokens(
  data,
  token = "token",
  time = "time",
  f0 = "f0",
  gap_ratio = 1.5,
  run = "voiced_run",
  min_f0 = 3,
  min_run = 1,
  flag = "screen_flag"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format: one row per f0 sample.

token, time, f0

Column names. Defaults "token", "time", "f0". time must be the real time column. f0 is the one column that decides which rows have f0.

gap_ratio

A time step longer than this many times the token's usual step is a gap. Default 1.5. Must be above 1. Inf reads gaps from rows without f0 only.

run

Name of a column that marks gaps already, such as the voiced_run column drop_rows_without_f0() adds. Default "voiced_run". Used only when the column is present. NULL ignores it.

min_f0

A token with fewer rows with f0 than this is flagged (reason 2). Default 3. Must be at least 1.

min_run

Samples a run at the start or end of a token must have to be counted, as in drop_rows_without_f0(). Default 1 counts every row with f0.

flag

Name of the column to add. Default "screen_flag". A column of that name already in data is replaced.

Value

data with the flag column, a character column, added or replaced, of the same class (a data frame or a tibble), with the rows in their original order and every other column as it was. Attribute flagged is a data frame with one row per flagged token, in order of first appearance in data: the token, in a column named as the token column, and reason, the text in the flag column. It has no rows when no token is flagged.

Details

Reasons, in this order, joined by "; ":

  1. "no f0": no row of the token has f0. No other reason is given.

  2. "only 2 samples with f0" or "only 1 sample with f0": fewer rows with f0 than min_f0 (with the default 3, 1 or 2 rows). A contour needs at least 3 points to show a turn. No other reason is given either, as such a token cannot be used whatever else is missing. With min_run above 1, the rows that drop_rows_without_f0() removes as short edge runs with the same min_run are not counted.

  3. Equal-point data only: "no f0 at the first point", "no f0 at the last point" or "no f0 at the first and last points".

  4. Equal-point data only: "3 points without f0 inside" or "1 point without f0 inside": every row without f0 between the token's first and last samples with f0, whatever the length of the gap.

Equal-point data. When there are at least two tokens and all have the same number of rows, as for 21 equidistant points from resampling, F0 Extraction or a Praat script (equal_rows in screen_f0_rows()), each token should have f0 at every point, so reasons 3 and 4 apply too, and the reasons say "points". In frame-by-frame data (tokens of different lengths), rows without f0 at a token's start or end or inside it are normal, and drop_rows_without_f0() removes them. So only reasons 1 and 2 apply, and the reasons say "samples".

The data as given. The reasons are read from data as it is. A row has no f0 when its value in the f0 column is NA, NaN or infinite; 0 and negative values count as f0 here. So run zero_hz_to_na() first, and set values such as -1 that a tracker writes for unvoiced frames to NA. Rows are taken in time order within each token, whatever their order in data. A row with no time (NA) counts in reason 2 when it has f0, but cannot be placed for reasons 3 and 4. A row whose token is NA belongs to a token of its own.

min_run. It changes reason 2 only when it is below min_f0: a token with a run of at least min_run samples keeps that run, and a token with no such run keeps all its samples. So with min_run = 3 and the default min_f0 = 3, the flags are the same as with min_run = 1.

See also

zero_hz_to_na() to run first; screen_f0_rows() for the counts; drop_rows_without_f0() to remove the rows without f0.

Examples

# 7 equidistant points per token
df <- data.frame(
  token = rep(c("a", "b", "c", "d"), each = 7),
  time  = rep(seq(0, 0.3, length.out = 7), 4),
  f0    = c(200, 205, 210, 215, 220, 225, 230,
            NA, 181, 183, NA, NA, NA, 190,
            NA, NA, 150, NA, NA, 154, NA,
            rep(NA, 7)))
# b misses its first point and 3 inside; c has only 2 points with f0,
# which is its only reason; d has no f0
out <- flag_f0_tokens(df)
unique(out[c("token", "screen_flag")])
#>    token                                          screen_flag
#> 1      a                                                     
#> 8      b no f0 at the first point; 3 points without f0 inside
#> 15     c                                only 2 points with f0
#> 22     d                                                no f0
attr(out, "flagged")
#>   token                                               reason
#> 1     b no f0 at the first point; 3 points without f0 inside
#> 2     c                                only 2 points with f0
#> 3     d                                                no f0
# Keep the tokens with no issue
out[out$screen_flag == "", ]
#>   token time  f0 screen_flag
#> 1     a 0.00 200            
#> 2     a 0.05 205            
#> 3     a 0.10 210            
#> 4     a 0.15 215            
#> 5     a 0.20 220            
#> 6     a 0.25 225            
#> 7     a 0.30 230            

# Frame-by-frame data: only too few samples with f0 count
fr <- data.frame(token = rep(c("x", "y"), c(8, 5)),
                 time  = c(1:8, 1:5) / 100,
                 f0    = c(NA, 200, 202, 204, NA, 206, 208, NA,
                           NA, 150, NA, 152, NA))
attr(flag_f0_tokens(fr), "flagged")
#>   token                 reason
#> 1     y only 2 samples with f0
